sections.label: Government acknowledges TraceTogether data error
sections.summary: The Government acknowledges its error in not stating that TraceTogether data is not exempt from the Criminal Procedure Code.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: The Government understands the difficulties faced by Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The Clerk will now proceed to read the Orders of the day.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We acknowledge our error in not stating that data from TraceTogether is not exempt from the Criminal Procedure Code.

sections.label: Restrictions on digital contact tracing data
sections.summary: Personal data from digital contact tracing systems can only be used for contact tracing, except for investigations or criminal proceedings in respect of serious offences.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The legislation specifies that personal data collected through digital contact tracing systems can only be used by public agencies for the specific purpose of contact tracing, except where there is a need to use that data for investigations or criminal proceedings in respect of serious offences.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We have decided that these restrictions will cover personal contact tracing data not only from TraceTogether, but also SafeEntry and a private sector system called BluePass insofar as BluePass is interoperable with TraceTogether.

sections.label: Contact tracing time shortened
sections.summary: TraceTogether and other digital contact tracing systems have shortened average contact tracing time from four days to less than 1.5 days.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: TraceTogether, alongside the other digital contact tracing systems, such as SafeEntry, has shortened the average time required for contact tracing from four days to now less than 1.5 days.

sections.label: Legislation covers personal contact tracing data
sections.summary: The legislation will cover personal contact tracing data recorded in any digital contact tracing system.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: First, the legislation will cover "personal contact tracing data" recorded in any "digital contact tracing system".

sections.label: Police access to contact tracing data
sections.summary: Police and law enforcement may not obtain personal contact tracing data except for investigations or criminal proceedings in respect of a serious offence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The Government's use of the data will be ring-fenced to contact tracing, with the exception for investigations or criminal proceedings in respect of serious offences.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Subsection 82(2) states that the Police and other law enforcement agencies "in the exercise of any power under the Criminal Procedure Code (Chapter 68) or other written law", may not obtain personal contact tracing data, except for "an investigation or criminal proceeding in respect of a serious offence".

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: There are seven categories of serious offences, set out, quite coincidentally, in the Seventh Schedule.

sections.label: Automatic purging of tracing data
sections.summary: TraceTogether devices and SafeEntry servers are purged automatically after 25 days unless data was extracted for contact tracing or serious offence investigations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Today, TraceTogether devices and SafeEntry servers are purged automatically after 25 days, unless that data has been extracted for contact tracing purposes or for the investigations or criminal proceedings in respect of serious offences.

sections.label: Extension of Act Part 7
sections.summary: Clause 2 extends Part 7 of the current Act for another year, until April 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Clause 2 of the Bill extends Part 7 of the current Act, for another year, until April 2022.

sections.label: SLA role and tracing data limits
sections.summary: Clause 4 amends Part 2A to set out SLA's role in the Rental Relief Framework, and the Government will limit use of personal contact tracing data except for investigations or criminal proceedings in serious offences.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Clause 4 of the Bill amends Part 2A of the Act to set out the Singapore Land Authority's (SLA's) role in the administration of the Rental Relief Framework.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: You will notice that it has been tightly scoped.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: It is a specific amendment made in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic – that the Government will limit its use of personal contact tracing data for the purposes of contact tracing, except where there is a need to do so for investigations or criminal proceedings in respect of serious offences.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We are introducing this Bill urgently, to remove any doubt among Singaporeans and to assure everyone that data will be properly safeguarded and used only for the appropriate purposes, so that we may continue to focus our attention towards battling this clear and present threat, the COVID-19 global pandemic.

sections.label: TraceTogether threshold and section 20
sections.summary: The 70% threshold was reportedly reached on 21 November 2020, and Minister Vivian Balakrishnan admitted in Parliament he did not consider section 20 of the Criminal Procedure Code at the next sitting on 5 January.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Since then and along with the issuance of TraceTogether tokens, this minimum 70% threshold was reportedly reached on 21 November 2020, even as it had been hovering around the 50% mark around two weeks earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: When Minister Vivian Balakrishnan admitted in Parliament that he did not consider section 20 of the Criminal Procedure Code at the next sitting of Parliament on 5 January this year, there are Singaporeans who opined that this was not fathomable or even believable for a largely efficient Government machinery that has consistently approached COVID-19 as a whole-of-Government endeavour.

sections.label: Eroded trust and exact date
sections.summary: The Government's handling has eroded trust from some members of the public, and it asks the exact date the Minister-in-charge of Smart Nation knew section 20 would apply to TraceTogether.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Whatever the view, it is apparent that the Government's handling of this matter has eroded trust from some members of the public.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, what was the exact date on which Minister-in-charge of Smart Nation knew that section 20 of the Criminal Procedure code would apply to TraceTogether?

sections.label: Questions on TraceTogether use
sections.summary: It asks the Minister whether the one known case where TraceTogether was used was solved and how critical the data was, and how many other times it was used for seven categories of serious crimes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To know whether these other tools are enough, I would like to ask the Minister two questions about the use of TraceTogether data for actual cases: (a) For the one known case where TraceTogether was used, was the case solved, in that a suspect has been identified or charged, and how critical was TraceTogether data to solving the case?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: (b) How many other times has TraceTogether been used for the seven categories of serious crimes so far?

sections.label: Signups and survey agreement
sections.summary: TraceTogether signups reached 80% from 78%, and an IPS report of 24 May 2020 found 87% of respondents agreeable to strict surveillance on those quarantined, but only 49% agreeable to cellphone data tracking without consent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the middle of last week, it was confirmed that the TraceTogether signups had reached 80% from 78% some weeks earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In an Institute of Policy Studies (IPS) report released on 24 May 2020, out of a broadly representative sample size of the Singaporean population, 87% of respondents were agreeable to imposing strict surveillance on those who needed to be quarantined.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But when the questioning moved to the employment of CCTVs and cellphones to prevent the spread of COVID-19, only 49% were agreeable to have their cellphone data tracked without their consent.

sections.label: Workers' Party supports TraceTogether Bill
sections.summary: The Workers' Party is prepared to support the Bill allowing TraceTogether data use for Police investigations in exceptional cases identified in the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Even so, the Workers' Party is prepared to support the Bill to allow for the use of TraceTogether data for Police investigations in the exceptional cases identified in the Bill.

sections.label: KPMG report on data concerns
sections.summary: A 2016 KPMG report found 32% of Singaporeans extremely concerned about personal data handling, and Singaporean consumers felt most defenceless among Asian respondents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A 2016 KPMG report shared that 32% of Singaporeans were extremely concerned about the handling and use of their personal data and that Singaporean consumers felt the most defenceless among Asian respondents over the way organisations handle and use their personal information.

sections.label: Prepare epidemic research programme
sections.summary: A new national research programme for epidemic preparedness and response called Prepare was announced in December 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In this regard, a new national research programme for epidemic preparedness and response called Prepare was announced in December 2020.

sections.label: MSF children's home analytics technology
sections.summary: The Government Financial Statements confirm the Ministry of Social and Family Development implemented video analytics, facial recognition and behavioural analytics at a voluntary children's home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Government Financial Statements confirm that the Ministry of Social and Family Development has implemented video analytics, facial recognition and behavioural analytics technology at a voluntary children's home.

sections.label: Facebook report on Singapore requests
sections.summary: The Straits Times reported in 2018 that Facebook's transparency report showed the Singapore Government made 244 requests concerning 310 accounts in late 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, the Straits Times reported in 2018 that Facebook's semi-annual transparency report revealed that the Singapore Government had made 244 request for information concerning 310 Facebook accounts in the latter half of 2017.

sections.label: CPC powers to access computers
sections.summary: Section 39 of the Criminal Procedure Code gives Police wide leeway to access computers and data, and Section 40 allows prosecutors to authorise accessing decryption information.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Section 39 of the Criminal Procedure Code, for example, gives the Police wide leeway when investigating arrestable offences to access computers and computer data, even for computers outside of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Section 40 of the CPC allows the public prosecutor to authorise the accessing of decryption information.

sections.label: Workers' Party support and privacy conversation
sections.summary: The Workers' Party supports the Bill while seeking answers on Police use of TraceTogether data and urging a national conversation on privacy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To recap, Sir, the Workers' Party is prepared to support the Bill even as we look forward to the Minister's answers on the specific queries with regard to the Police's use of TraceTogether data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But, separately, and arising from this episode, I urge the Government to open a national conversation on privacy forthwith, with a view to not just prevent the weakening of trust between citizens and the state today, but to strengthen it for the Singapore of tomorrow.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Speaker, Sir, today's debate on the COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) (Amendment) Bill is very meaningful.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: This amendment, essentially, restricts the use of information collected by TraceTogether and SafeEntry to seven serious crimes.

sections.label: Singapore employment and fixed investments
sections.summary: Local employment in Singapore has returned to pre-COVID-19 levels and Singapore attracted $17.2 billion in fixed investments last year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Despite that COVID-19 has dealt a severe blow to the global economy and livelihoods around the world, local employment in Singapore has finally returned to pre-COVID-19 levels, even attracting $17.2 billion in fixed investments last year, which is 13% higher than in 2019.

sections.label: Bill defines seven serious crimes
sections.summary: The Bill defines the seven serious crimes where TraceTogether data can be used outside of contact tracing purposes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: The Bill defines the seven serious crimes where TraceTogether data can be used outside of contact tracing purposes.

sections.label: Police use for missing person cases
sections.summary: The passage asks whether Police can use TraceTogether data for cases outside the seven categories, such as a missing person case.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: First, after this Bill is passed, if there were other type of cases outside of the seven categories, such as a missing person case, the Police will be under immense pressure to solve it, will the Police be able to use the data from TraceTogether?

sections.label: Hesitation to use TraceTogether
sections.summary: Some people may still hesitate to use TraceTogether even after this Bill is passed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Perhaps, even after this Bill is passed, some people would still hesitate to use TraceTogether.

sections.label: Confidence and fight against COVID-19
sections.summary: The passage states that confidence exists that any storm can be overcome and that the fight against COVID-19 must not be given up.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: They give us confidence that no matter how severe the storm is, we can overcome it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Therefore, we must not give up our fight against COVID-19 at this juncture.

sections.label: Privacy sacrifice for public safety
sections.summary: The speaker says restricting TraceTogether use trades a bit of privacy for public safety and health, and hopes everyone supports the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Given that the Bill has restricted the use of TraceTogether information, sacrificing a bit of privacy in exchange for public safety and health can be seen as a good deed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: I hope that everyone will support this Bill.

sections.label: Seven offence categories for TraceTogether
sections.summary: The Bill ensures Police can use TraceTogether data only under seven categories of offences, which the speaker supports to keep contact tracing the purpose.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: What this Bill does is ensure that only under these seven categories of offences can the Police use the TraceTogether data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I support this because in limiting to these seven categories, it allows the raison d'etre continues to be contact tracing.

sections.label: Drug offence death sentence limit
sections.summary: The speaker notes TraceTogether data can be used for drug-related offences only if they attract a death sentence, and would not have so restricted it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: If you look under the fourth offence, which is the drug-related offence, the TraceTogether data can only be used if the offence attracts a death sentence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I know I am pushing the envelope here, but because of my strong stance against drug trafficking, the heinous nature of the offence and the multi-generational effects it causes on families, if it were up to me, I would not have restricted it to only crimes which attract a death sentence.

sections.label: Retrospective tracing versus real time
sections.summary: The speaker says the Bill may unintentionally allow only retrospective tracing of known drug trafficking, not real time tracing, and guesses CNB and stakeholders collectively decided the death sentence restriction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In effect, the Bill may have the unintended effect of only allowing retrospective tracing and not real time tracing of known drug trafficking whereas, in my view, real time tracing could create more leads thereby making CNB operations more efficient and productive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: My guess is that CNB was consulted in this along with the stakeholders – AGC, MHA, MCI and SNDGO, and the collective decision was to restrict it to only to death sentence for drug-related offences.

sections.label: Seven categories strike right balance
sections.summary: The speaker says the seven categories strike the right balance, supports the Bill, and says the furore could have been avoided with clearer Government communication.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The seven categories listed in the Bill strike the right balance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: And for these reasons, I support the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, it seems to me that the furore about the use of TraceTogether data could have been avoided if the Government had been clear from the start that the Police would be using its powers to access the data.

sections.label: Limits to seven serious crimes
sections.summary: The Bill limits Police use of TraceTogether data to seven categories of serious crimes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Third, the Bill limits Police's use of TraceTogether data to seven categories of serious crimes.

sections.label: Seventh Schedule amendment limits
sections.summary: The Bill states the Seventh Schedule can only be amended by Parliament through the main Act, not by Subsidiary Legislation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Bill makes clear that the Seventh Schedule cannot be amended by Subsidiary Legislation but only through amending the main Act in Parliament.

sections.label: TraceTogether device data transient
sections.summary: TraceTogether data on devices is encrypted, stored for only 25 days, then automatically deleted.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To this end, we understand that TraceTogether data on devices is transient as it is encrypted and stored for only 25 days, after which it is automatically deleted.

sections.label: TraceTogether contact tracing only
sections.summary: On 4 June 2020, the Government answered that TraceTogether data would be used for contact tracing only.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: On 4 June 2020, the Government's answer was that the data from TraceTogether would be used for contact tracing only.

sections.label: TraceTogether data for police investigations
sections.summary: The Bill seeks permission for TraceTogether and SafeEntry data to be available to Police for criminal investigations into seven categories of serious offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It was an error, in the words of Minister Vivian Balakrishnan, a mea culpa that arose because it was not drawn to his attention that the Criminal Procedure Code (CPC) was applicable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This Bill asks for permission to make TraceTogether and SafeEntry data, which was meant to be used for contact tracing to be available to the Police when there is a clear and pressing need to use that data for criminal investigations into seven categories of serious offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: One point that was made was that the Police has already an abundance of tools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: But, to me, I find it useful that in this Bill, there is the operative words "clear and pressing need", and that, to me, limits the ability to use the data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: And in relation to the seven categories – these are serious crimes that we are talking about – anyone looking at it would know that – and I am, in a sense, sharing what I am going to say a bit later – in balancing privacy concerns with really the concern for meting out justice in relation to the commission of serious offences, the Police should be provided access.

sections.label: Bill compromise for contact tracing
sections.summary: The Bill is a compromise to avoid losing quick contact tracing via TraceTogether and SafeEntry during the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The crucial point to note is that this Bill represents a compromise to ensure that we do not take the risk of losing the ability to conduct contact tracing quickly and aggressively via TraceTogether and SafeEntry when we are in the midst of a pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It seems to me that there is broad agreement for data to be used to investigate the seven categories of serious crime proposed under the Bill.

sections.label: Extending categories risks adoption
sections.summary: Extending the categories would gamble on whether Singaporeans and residents still adopt TraceTogether and SafeEntry or are put off.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Extending the categories will require hon Members of this House to take a gamble on whether or not a group of Singaporeans and residents will still be prepared to adopt TraceTogether and SafeEntry – and that is a point that the hon Leader of Opposition made – or, instead, be put off in light of the extended use of the data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This is not a gamble that we should take, given the state of COVID-19 pandemic today.

sections.label: Safety and contact tracing
sections.summary: The Member suggests stepping back to consider what the easy way out is, saying the bigger issue is population safety and successful contact tracing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: I would suggest, very respectfully, to the hon Member that we have to take a step back and look at what is this easy way out of.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: And, in my humble view, the bigger issue is to ensure the safety of the population at hand and to ensure that contact tracing is successful.

sections.label: Government position on serious crimes
sections.summary: The Member accepts serious crimes must be looked at carefully but says Government should explain how critical TraceTogether information is.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: In this context, Government has put out a position and I would accept, as I have, that serious crimes are something that we have to look at carefully.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: But it is important, I think, for the Government to explain how critical TraceTogether information actually is.

sections.label: Purpose of TraceTogether Bill
sections.summary: The Member says the Bill's purpose is TraceTogether and doubts drug lords or criminals carry TraceTogether tokens and applications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: But if one thinks about it, we have to bring ourselves back down to the purpose of this Bill which is TraceTogether.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: And the simple answer to that is I do not think drug lords or criminals will be carrying TraceTogether tokens and TraceTogether applications around.

sections.label: Police powers over TraceTogether data
sections.summary: Minister of State Desmond Tan said the Singapore Police Force is empowered under the Criminal Procedure Code to obtain TraceTogether data for criminal investigations, and assured the House data is secure and only authorised officers access it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Minister of State Desmond Tan said that, "The Singapore Police Force is empowered under the Criminal Procedure Code or CPC to obtain any data, including TraceTogether or TT data for criminal investigations", and went on to assure the House that the data was secure and only authorised officers are allowed to access it.

sections.label: TraceTogether privacy statement change
sections.summary: The Member says the Smart Nation Digital Government Office announced legislative provisions three days later, and the privacy statement's absolute assurance changed only after the PQ was answered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Three days later, on 8 January, the Smart Nation Digital Government Office announced upcoming legislative provisions for the usage of data from TT and SafeEntry, which are in the Bill we are debating today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: All that time the TT's privacy statement contained a more absolute assurance and, I quote, "Any data shared with MOH will only be used solely for contact tracing of persons possibly exposed to COVID-19." This privacy statement changed only sometime after 12.25 pm on 4 January, the afternoon that the PQ was answered, with the new clarification that it can also be used for criminal investigations.

sections.label: SafeEntry access and sunset clause
sections.summary: The Member says SafeEntry data is also accessible to the Police, and the sunset clause gives the Minister much power over digital contact tracing and data deletion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, we now know that SafeEntry data is also accessible to the Police.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Second, the sunset clause proposed under section 82(8) gives a lot of power to the Minister to determine if we still need digital contact tracing and when the contact tracing data will be deleted.

sections.label: Contact tracing data safeguards question
sections.summary: An MP asks whether section 82 safeguards cover MOH contact tracing data and whether Police access continues after the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Third, do the safeguards in section 82 of the Bill cover data that has been uploaded to MOH databases for the purposes of contact tracing?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If so, will the Police still be allowed to access this data even after the pandemic is over?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I asked a similar question on 5 January and the Minister answered then, "I believe that once the pandemic has passed, that data – certainly the specific personalised data – those fields should be eliminated." Can I confirm that this remains the intent of this Bill?

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: In relation to how I got the impression that the powers would only be used when there is a clear and pressing need, I would like to direct her attention to the Government statement issued on 8 January 2021, entitled "Upcoming Legislative Provisions for Usage of Data from Digital Contact Tracing Solutions", where in paragraph three, it is stated that the legislation will specify the personal data collected through digital contact tracing solutions which comprise the TraceTogether programme and SafeEntry programme can only be used for the specific purpose of contact tracing except where there is a clear and pressing need to use that data for criminal investigations of serious offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: So, that is how I formed the impression and I would invite the hon Minister to confirm if my impression is correct, in his response to us.

sections.label: Token data safeguards
sections.summary: The Minister said safeguards include keeping data on the token and deleting it after 25 days.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The Minister had also shared that there are safeguards and what these safeguards include – that the data is kept on the token and is also deleted after 25 days.

sections.label: TraceTogether stood down after pandemic
sections.summary: The Minister said TraceTogether will be stood down after the pandemic and personal contact tracing data deleted as soon as practicable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The Minister in his speech also shared that when the pandemic is over, the TraceTogether solution will be stood down and all personal digital contact tracing data used for COVID-19 contact tracing will be deleted from the systems as soon as practicable.

sections.label: Bill restricts contact tracing data use
sections.summary: The Bill allows Sixth Schedule TraceTogether and SafeEntry data only for COVID-19 contact tracing, except for serious offences in the Seventh Schedule.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: If this Bill is passed, it will mean that personal contact data from TraceTogether and SafeEntry as set out in the Sixth Schedule of the Bill can only be used for COVID-19 contact tracing purpose when there is an infection and the only exception will be when the data is needed for criminal investigation proceedings for the serious offences as specified in the Seventh Schedule of the Bill.

sections.label: Timely data for serious crimes
sections.summary: For serious crimes like murder, terrorism or kidnapping, timely data access could mean the difference between life and death.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: In situations involving serious crimes – and the list, I think, we have all talked about that, in terms of the seriousness of those crimes – like murder, terrorism or kidnapping, timely access to data could make the difference between life and death.

sections.label: Lost token criminal use
sections.summary: An MP asks what happens if someone loses their token and another person uses it for criminal purposes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: As the Bill seeks to allow for personal contact tracing data to be accessed by the Police to assist in the investigation of serious crimes, what will happen if someone loses his/her token and it is used by another person for criminal purposes?

sections.label: Contact tracing data use limits
sections.summary: The Bill seeks to clarify use and limits of COVID-19 contact tracing data for tracing and criminal investigations, balancing public health, safety and privacy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The measures proposed in this Bill are important as they seek to make clear the use and the limitations of personal contact tracing data for COVID-19 contact tracing purposes and criminal investigations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: It is a balance between public health and keeping everyone in Singapore safe and secure while respecting personal privacy.

sections.label: Support for the Bill
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Bill for the reasons given and the public safety implications shared.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: For these reasons, Mr Speaker, and for the implications that I have shared on public safety, I support the Bill.

sections.label: Broken trust over TraceTogether data
sections.summary: Trust in Government promises that TraceTogether data would only be used for contact tracing was broken when police accessed it for a murder investigation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But in the end, our people trusted both Minister Balakrishnan's and Senior Minister Teo's promises that the collected data would only be used for contact tracing, which was why TraceTogether adoption finally surpassed 70% in December 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This trust was broken during the January parliamentary session, when not only did the Government admitted that TraceTogether data was accessible to the Singapore Police Force for the purposes of criminal investigations, it was already actually assessed by the Police to investigate a murder.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This broken promise has broken the public's trust in the Government.

sections.label: PSP opposes the Bill
sections.summary: The Progress Singapore Party opposes the Bill, saying proceeding without answering questions leaves doubts about rebuilding trust or rubber stamping police actions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: To proceed with this Bill, without answering these questions will leave serious doubts in the public's mind over whether this Bill is truly to rebuild public trust in a Government or to rubber stamp the Police actions after the fact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It is therefore in the spirit of rebuilding public trust that the Progress Singapore Party rises in opposition to this Bill.

sections.label: Benefit of 25-day data
sections.summary: The passage asks how much incremental benefit comes from a set of data that exists only for 25 days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: How much is the incremental benefit, from a set of data that exists only for 25 days?

sections.label: PSP opposes, cites Australia, trade-off
sections.summary: The Progress Singapore Party opposes the Bill, cites Australia's legislation, and says it would not trade a child's life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Australian government has publicly committed that the data collected by the contact tracing application cannot be accessed by the Police and is to be used only for contact tracing purposes, and has already passed legislation to that effect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Any action the Government takes to deal with this pandemic be it to prioritise public health and trust or public safety will significantly impact our people's trust and confidence in the Government's action in future pandemics and other unforeseen calamities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, when all the various issues are considered, passing this Bill may actually run against the Government's objective of rallying everybody together to fight the pandemic which should be our top priority at this moment in time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Progress Singapore Party therefore stands opposed against this Bill and calls upon the Government to keep to his original promise by fully exempting contact tracing data from the CPC.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development and Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: So, would I be correct then in understanding that, in the example given by Minister Vivian, that if there was a child kidnapped and let us say, there is no other sign of any evidence, the only thing that you have is TraceTogether data, Mr Leong's position would be, "No, let it be, we will not access that data." Is it that the position?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: But of course, in any of the decisions we make, there is a trade-off.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: So, when you take the position of the Bill what you are saying public trust plus the needs of public health – both of these benefits would be less than the benefits that you draw or you expect to draw from public safety.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: So, we have the weigh the trade-off and after weighing the trade-off, we hold the stand that we are going against this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: There is a trade-off, but we would not trade a child's life for something like that.

sections.label: Singapore police force size
sections.summary: Singapore has just under 9,700 regular police officers, around 170 per 100,000 people, compared with the US, Hong Kong and Malaysia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Singapore's Police Force is small, relative to the population.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We have just under 9,700 regular police officers in Singapore, which is around 170 per 100,000 people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: For example, the US has around 238, Hong Kong has 487 and Malaysia has around 320.

sections.label: Public trust and police powers
sections.summary: People trust the Police and expect crimes solved, reflected in section 20 of the Criminal Procedure Code allowing certain officers to order production of documents or things.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: People share information freely with the Police, trust the Police and expect them to be able to solve crimes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This expectation is reflected in section 20 of the Criminal Procedure Code which allows a Police officer above the rank of sergeant to order a person to "produce any document or thing" to assist in investigations.

sections.label: Limitation on police evidence powers
sections.summary: The limitation applies only to Police powers, not Court powers, and with 25 days to gather evidence, upfront decisions matter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I understand that this limitation is only to the powers of the Police and not to the powers of the Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: But in practical terms, where you only have 25 days to gather this evidence, if the decision is not made upfront to gather this evidence, it is unlikely to be gathered or used in Court.

sections.label: TraceTogether data for serious crime
sections.summary: TraceTogether data can currently be used for serious crime, but not for matters such as sexual assault, non-grievous violence or non-capital drug offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Currently, TraceTogether data can be used for serious crime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: For example, if sexual assault is not serious, it cannot be used; violence not amounting to grievous bodily harm non-capital drug offences.

sections.label: SafeEntry data use restrictions
sections.summary: Police are now prevented from using SafeEntry data for anything apart from serious matters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Police are also being prevented from using SafeEntry data now for anything apart from serious matters.

sections.label: Privacy concerns and Bill compromise
sections.summary: The speaker acknowledges privacy concerns limit use in crime fighting, has reservations on the restrictions, but supports the Bill as a compromise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: But I do acknowledge that there are people who have concerns about privacy and therefore its use in crime fighting is going to be limited.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, yes, I do have my reservations on these restrictions, but as this Bill is a compromise, I support it.

sections.label: TraceTogether data use concerns
sections.summary: TraceTogether boosts contact tracing and over 4.2 million enrolled, but some Singaporeans have concerns about expanded use of TT data under CPC investigation powers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The positive impact of TraceTogether, or TT for short, in increasing the efficiency of our contact tracing efforts is undeniable but given the developments since we last sat in this House last month, we must also understand the sentiments of some Singaporeans about the expanded use of TT data in connection with the investigation powers under the CPC beyond what was originally promised to be used solely for contact tracing purposes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While we note the strict conditions in which the data can be accessed, the very collection and storage of such information does involve an ideological leap in some quarters.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, many believed in the purpose for which the data would be used and on that basis more than 4.2 million people have enrolled in the programme today.

sections.label: TT data and holding charges
sections.summary: Asks how cases are handled when the eventual charge falls outside serious offence categories, and whether TT data use pressures prosecutors toward holding charges.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: How will we deal with cases where TT data is used in investigations where the actual charge, in the end, does not fall within the categories of these serious offences?

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Will the use of TT data during investigations put pressure on prosecutors to proceed with a holding charge for a more serious offence in order to legitimise the use of TT data?

sections.label: Usefulness of 25-day TT data
sections.summary: Asks how useful TT data is for investigations given it is automatically deleted in 25 days and very little actual information is collected and stored.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Given that TT data is automatically deleted in 25 days and very little actual information is collected and stored, how useful is this data for investigations?

sections.label: Condition to end TT programme
sections.summary: Suggests one condition could be that with no new community or imported infections for a number of months, the TT programme will be laid to rest.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As an example, one of the "conditions" could be, should there be no new infections, both community and imported, for a period of x number of months, the TT programme will then be laid to rest.

sections.label: TT data protocols and evidence utility
sections.summary: Notes TT protocols like encryption, local storage and 25-day destruction were for contact tracing, but sees utility as evidence for grave offences; many Singaporeans accept investigation use.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It is evident to me that the various protocols around the TT data, for example, encryption, storage on local device and the automatic destruction after 25 days, were in place solely for contact tracing purposes at the time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, as a lawyer, I also understand the potential utility for which the TT data could bring as evidence, in particular, for grave offences, and the potential to charge an accused who committed a wrongdoing, exonerate someone who is innocent, and give peace to victims and their families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Based on several conversations I have had on the ground, many Singaporeans understand and are willing for TT data to be used in investigations although some do wish that they had been consulted first.

sections.label: Call to exempt TraceTogether data
sections.summary: Prefers the Government completely exempt TraceTogether data from Criminal Procedure Code provisions, as the surest way to maintain trust and match original communications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: And therefore, the Government must do all it can to continue keeping trust with our people in this fight.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: This is why personally, I would much prefer – much prefer – that the Government maintains what it had communicated at the start, at the outset, and completely exempts TraceTogether data from Criminal Procedure Code provisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: In my view, this is the surest way – not the only way but the surest way – to maintain the trust between Government and people that is so crucial in this fight, and the surest way to help Singaporeans understand what Minister Balakrishnan himself had referred to in his clarifications in this House last month, and I quote "not only the measures that we are implementing, but why we are implementing it, the spirit behind it." A complete exemption of TraceTogether data from Criminal Procedure Code provisions, in line with the Government's original communications on this matter would, in my view, be the surest way to achieve this.

sections.label: TraceTogether data purge timeline
sections.summary: TraceTogether data will still be automatically purged after 25 days and cease to exist once the pandemic ends, despite the proposed legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, they understand the Government’s thinking on this matter and recognise the Government’s practical and calibrated approach on this matter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: And I note that TraceTogether data, as it was originally designed, will ultimately continue to be automatically purged after 25 days and cease to exist altogether once this pandemic is behind us, the proposed legislation notwithstanding.

sections.label: Support for calibrated security Bill
sections.summary: After considering the Minister's clarifications, personal views and residents' views, the speaker is prepared to support the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: On the other, having a calibrated way to also enhance public security and safety.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: I thought long and hard about this matter and, ultimately, after considering the Minister's clarifications, my personal views and by listening to the whole range of views amongst my residents, I am prepared to support this Bill.

sections.label: Trust in Police, TraceTogether furore
sections.summary: The speaker trusts the Police and was surprised at the furore over TraceTogether data possibly being used in Police investigations under the Criminal Procedure Code.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I trust them with my life, I trust them to keep us safe, and I trust that they take their responsibility and duty diligently.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I must admit that I was a little surprised at the furore over the revelation that TraceTogether data may be used in Police investigations under the Criminal Procedure Code.

sections.label: Trust broken by expanded use
sections.summary: Being told the data will be used beyond its original intention feels like trust has been broken.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: To be then told it will also be used for something beyond the original intention feels like trust has been broken.

sections.label: Rectify mistake and reassure public
sections.summary: The Government must rectify the mistake, apologise for the miscommunication, acknowledge concerns, understand discontentment and reassure the public on preventing similar future occurrences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: What the Government must do now is to rectify this mistake, apologise for the miscommunication, acknowledge the concerns that have been raised, understand the reasons for the discontentment, and reassure the public on what will be done to prevent similar occurrences for future policies.

sections.label: Reservations on limiting Police powers
sections.summary: Like Mr Vikram Nair, the speaker has reservations on the legislation restraining Police investigative powers and limiting the crimes the data can be used for.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: As with the hon Member Mr Vikram Nair, I have reservations on this legislation that we are placing a restraint on the Police's investigative powers and limiting the type of crimes that the data can be used for.

sections.label: TraceTogether communication and broken trust
sections.summary: The speaker says unhappiness stems from broken trust and a perceived lack of transparency in communicating TraceTogether's use, and that the Government should have been more open.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This has helped us tremendously in combating the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I note from feedback and conversations with residents who are volunteers and many others that the unhappiness does not stem from the Police access to the data but from a broken trust – from the sense that trust has been broken, that a promise was not kept.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The problem really lies with the omission of information and a perceived lack of transparency to the public on communication regarding the use of TraceTogether.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Certainly, the Government should have been more open, more prepared and more diligent about communicating this aspect to the public.

sections.label: TraceTogether as temporary extraordinary measure
sections.summary: The speaker states that these are extraordinary times and that TraceTogether is an extraordinary, temporary tool.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: These are extraordinary times and TraceTogether is an extraordinary measure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: It is a temporary tool and that bears repeating.

sections.label: Police investigations and CPC reach
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether TraceTogether data should be treated as another source for police investigations or excluded from the CPC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: This is how police investigations have operated over the years and contribute to making our Police Force effective.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Now that the Ministry has clarified the reach of CPC, do we treat TT data as another source of information that can be used by our Police Force in the course of their investigations?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Or are we trying to say that certain sets of data and sources of information should be excluded from CPC, and hence cannot be used by the Police Force to help them in the course of their investigations?

sections.label: Limiting TraceTogether data to seven offences
sections.summary: The speaker says allowing TraceTogether data only for seven offence categories means it cannot easily be used as evidence for other crimes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: (In Malay):   When we allow TT data to be used only for these seven categories of criminal offences, we should do so with an awareness of its implications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: This essentially means that, after excluding these seven crimes, TT data cannot be easily used as evidence to prosecute or to defend those suspected of crimes that are not included in these seven categories.

sections.label: Balancing privacy, health, safety and justice
sections.summary: The speaker says privacy must be balanced against public health, safety, security and justice, and notes TraceTogether data is stored only up to 25 days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: (In English): Mdm Deputy Speaker, while I understand the concerns of personal privacy, the challenge that we are facing is that we have to balance between privacy, public health and safety, security and justice – a point also mentioned by fellow Members Mr de Souza, Mr Murali, Ms Tan and Minister Vivian.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We must also not lose sight of the designed principles of TT and the fact that TraceTogether data is stored only up to 25 days.

sections.label: Bill limits data use, speaker supports
sections.summary: The speaker says the Bill limits data use to seven serious offence categories, that helpful information should be available to Police, and supports the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In this case, the Bill limits the use of such data to these seven categories of serious criminal offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Information that may assist in investigation, even if it is remotely helpful, should be made available to the Police.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding the arguments above, Mdm Deputy Speaker, I support this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One month after this issue first arose in Parliament, we are now debating a piece of legislation introduced on a Certificate of Urgency to put in safeguards on the use of data.

sections.label: TraceTogether data use protocols
sections.summary: Asks the Minister to explain operational protocols ensuring TraceTogether data used for serious crimes is not used for less serious crimes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, can Minister explain what operational protocols are in place to ensure TraceTogether data used for serious crimes do not become used for investigations of less serious crimes?

sections.label: Debate impact on TraceTogether use
sections.summary: States the past month's debate may have affected actual TraceTogether app use, with reports of people turning it off, and that the effect must be measured.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Second, the debate over the past month may have impacted actual use of the TraceTogether app.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We already know from newspaper reports that some people are now choosing to turn off their TraceTogether app when meeting friends or when going out; we must measure the precise effect of such changes.

sections.label: Compliance rate data analysis
sections.summary: Asks the Minister to share what data analysis traces whether actual compliance with TraceTogether app requirements does not go down.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For public health reasons, can the Minister share what specific data analysis is used to trace whether actual compliance rate with TraceTogether app requirements does not go down?

sections.label: Bill restricts contact tracing data access
sections.summary: States the Bill bars any public officer from accessing contact tracing data, except Police investigations restricted to seven serious offences specified in the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For future threats and serious crimes, it behoves the Police to utilise all the tools at its disposal to detect and prevent such crimes and it is incumbent upon us, as Members of this House to facilitate this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This Bill specifies that the contact tracing data cannot be accessed by any public officer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The only exception is for Police investigations and this is further restricted to the seven serious offences specified in the Bill.

sections.label: Offences against children and vulnerable persons
sections.summary: Asks the Ministry to consider including crimes against children under 14 or vulnerable persons as serious offences in the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: While I agree that these seven categories are egregious offences, I would like to ask the Ministry to consider that crimes or offences against children under the age 14 or vulnerable persons, to be considered as offences that are serious enough to be included in this Bill.

sections.label: Court order for exceptional cases
sections.summary: Suggests leaving the door open for Police to seek a specific Court order to use data in exceptional cases, especially offences against children or specific groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Perhaps we should leave the door slightly open for the Police or the law enforcement agencies to seek a specific Court order to allow the use of data in exceptional cases, especially when it will help to investigate offences committed against children or specific groups.

sections.label: Public confidence in TraceTogether
sections.summary: The two objectives are not mutually exclusive, and public confidence in TraceTogether and SafeEntry remains because it helped contain the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, the two objectives are not mutually exclusive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I believe that there is still great public confidence in TraceTogether and SafeEntry, because it has helped us to contain the spread of the pandemic in our country effectively.

sections.label: Temporary compromise on data privacy
sections.summary: The debate will shape future privacy issues; the legislation is a temporary compromise drawing a clear line on Police use of TraceTogether records.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: (In English): Mdm Deputy Speaker, this debate will shape how we treat other issues surrounding privacy of data in the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This legislation, however, is a temporary compromise, at least until the pandemic is over and it makes clear what can or cannot be used by the Police in its investigations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I am glad that we have that line drawn clearly in the sand, before we cross too far and get lost in the desert.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: With that, Mdm Deputy Speaker, I support this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   Mdm Deputy Speaker, thank you for the opportunity to speak on this Amendment Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I agree that the Government respects Singaporeans' desire for personal data privacy, and make it clear that unless it is for the investigation of seven categories of serious offenses set out in the Bill, the authorities will not use or share any records in TraceTogether.

sections.label: Strict protocol for tracing data
sections.summary: Contact tracing data should be used only in the most dire circumstances, like the seven serious offences, with a strict and transparent protocol.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: (In English): In summary, Mdm Deputy Speaker, while I speak in support of using any available digital contact tracing technology, including TraceTogether tokens and SafeEntry records to assist in criminal investigations, I also recognise the fact that its primary intention and objective was to serve the purpose of preventing COVID-19 clusters from manifesting in our community.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I therefore agree that we should reserve the right to use contract tracing data only in the most dire of circumstances, like the seven categories of serious offences as set out in the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: If and when it is necessary to utilise under such circumstances, I urge the relevant authorities, while handling such data, to adhere to a strict and transparent protocol throughout the entire process, from its retrieval for usage to its eventual disposal.

sections.label: Access after 25-day deletion
sections.summary: The Bill provides a white-list limiting TraceTogether data to seven serious crimes, and asks if Police can access data after 25 days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Singaporeans understand and support the need to fight crime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It is, therefore, reassuring that we are now moving this Bill to provide a “white-list”, limiting the use of TraceTogether data to seven categories of serious crimes and nothing else.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: To provide further reassurance, can the Minister elaborate if the Police are still able to access the TraceTogether data after it has been collected for 25 days?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In a criminal investigation, the Police may want to trace back a suspect’s movements well longer than 25 days ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In this instance, would they be able to recover, retrieve and access the data even after deletion?

sections.label: Opposition to special treatment
sections.summary: The speaker is not in favour of special treatment for TraceTogether data and says its use should be authorised even for non-listed crimes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Today, we are gathered here to debate whether legislation should be passed to limit the use of TraceTogether data by police and courts to only the investigation of seven types of serious crimes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Frankly, I am not in favour of this "special treatment" for TraceTogether data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In my view, even if a crime is not under the seven categories of serious crimes, the use of the data should be authorised for police investigations or court proceedings.

sections.label: Community interest over individual
sections.summary: Singapore should not become like western countries where privacy protection leaves cases unsolved, as Asian society values community interest over individual.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We should not become like some western developed countries where certain cases cannot be solved due to privacy protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We are an Asian society where the interest of the community is more important than that of the individual.

sections.label: Contact tracing data prosecution limits
sections.summary: The Police and Prosecution cannot use contact tracing data to prosecute a non-serious offence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: The Police and Prosecution will not be able to use the contact tracing data for prosecution of a non-serious offence.

sections.label: Police TraceTogether data request
sections.summary: The Police requested TraceTogether data once for a May 2020 murder, but the suspect's phone had no app, so no useful data was obtained.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: The Police have only requested for TT data once, for a murder that occurred in May 2020, in line with their powers under the CPC.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: As the TT app was not installed in the suspect’s phone, there was no useful data obtained.

sections.label: CPC framework police effectiveness
sections.summary: The current CPC framework has enabled the Police to work efficiently and effectively, keeping Singapore safe and secure.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Our current framework under the CPC has enabled the Police to do their job efficiently and effectively, and Singapore has thus been kept safe and secure.

sections.label: Inspector rank for contact tracing requests
sections.summary: Requests for contact tracing data must be made by an officer of Inspector rank and above, higher than the CPC's sergeant requirement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: First, while the Criminal Procedure Code, or CPC, specifies that production orders can only be made by officers with the rank of sergeant and above, we, in fact, intend to require the rank of requesting officer for contact tracing data to be higher.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: All requests for contact tracing data will have to be made by an officer of Inspector rank and above.

sections.label: Disclosure order for serious offences
sections.summary: The receiving party must comply with an order to disclose data to the Police only if it relates to a serious offence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: Third, the receiving party will only be required to comply with the order to disclose the data to the Police, if it is in relation to a serious offence.

sections.label: Serious sexual crimes definition
sections.summary: Under serious sexual crimes, only rape and sexual assault with penetration are covered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: On Ms Sylvia Lim's question regarding what is included under the category of serious sexual crimes, only rape and sexual assault with penetration will be covered.

sections.label: Shortened period to one and a half days
sections.summary: The speaker reiterates that something has been shortened from four days to one and a half days.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: In particular, I would reiterate that it has enabled us to shorten the period from four days to one and a half days.

sections.label: CPC applied and Police request
sections.summary: The speaker was informed that the CPC applied and that Police had requested TraceTogether data once before.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: At that point, I was informed that the CPC applied and that in fact, the Police had requested TraceTogether data on one previous occasion.

sections.label: Reflection and three categories
sections.summary: The speaker says he should have been aware and clear from the onset, reflects on adding four words in June, and lists three categories to address.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: But I should have been aware and I should have made it clear right from the onset.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I have reflected that if in June, I had added four words – subject to prevailing legislation – perhaps we would not be here this afternoon.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I want to, in the rest of this wrap-up speech, address the different queries, comments and suggestions under three categories: first, trust and participation in digital contact tracing; second, the technical features and safeguards of TraceTogether and SafeEntry; and third, to deal with the specific clarifications of clauses within the Bill.

sections.label: Bill on contact tracing data use
sections.summary: The Bill ensures personal digital contact tracing data can only be used for contact tracing, with a narrow exception for investigations and criminal proceedings in seven categories of serious offences.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Today, I come before this House, moving legislation on a Certificate of Urgency to give legal force to the statements that the Minister for Home Affairs and I made in Parliament last month.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: This Bill ensures that personal digital contact tracing data can only be used for contact tracing, with a narrow exception for investigations and criminal proceedings in respect of seven categories of serious offences.

sections.label: 350 deletions and 390,000 onboard
sections.summary: In one month, 350 individuals asked to delete their data while over 390,000 joined the TraceTogether programme.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: In the last one month, we have had 350 individuals who have asked us to delete their data – 350.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: At least 350 have, for a variety of reasons, decided to forgo the protection that TraceTogether offers them and their loved ones.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: But on the other hand, in this same period, in this same one month, over 390,000 have come onboard the TraceTogether programme.

sections.label: Over 80% onboard programme
sections.summary: More than 80% of Singapore residents are onboard the programme.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Today, more than 80% of Singapore residents are onboard the programme.

sections.label: TraceTogether data use limits
sections.summary: The Bill limits Government use of TraceTogether data to contact tracing, except for investigations and criminal proceedings on serious offences, regardless of access or sharing.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: We send you a PIN, you have to enter the PIN before the data is uploaded.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: This Bill limits the Government's use of TraceTogether data to the purposes of contact tracing with the exception, as I said earlier, for investigations and criminal proceedings in respect of serious offences, and it applies regardless of how the data is accessed or shared.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Users can do so and we have done so, as I shared just now; we have deleted data for 350 persons in the last one month.

sections.label: SafeEntry and BluePass covered
sections.summary: The Bill brings SafeEntry and BluePass, where they interoperate with TraceTogether, within the same protective cocoon.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Nevertheless, we have decided in this Bill to envelope SafeEntry and BluePass insofar as it interoperates with TraceTogether within the same protective cocoon that this Bill provides.

sections.label: Bill limits agencies, not individuals
sections.summary: The Bill circumscribes public sector agencies' use of personal contact tracing data but does not prohibit individuals from using or requesting their own data if entitled.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: The Bill circumscribes the use of personal contact tracing data by public sector agencies, but I will reiterate, does not prohibit individuals from using or requesting for their own personal contact tracing data provided they have a right to access such data.

sections.label: Section 82(7) access rights
sections.summary: Section 82(7) lets individuals keep access to personal contact tracing data if they have such a right under any rule of law or otherwise.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Again, the criminal lawyers here will understand what I am talking about.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: This is in the Bill – specifically, section 82(7) allows for individuals to continue to have access to personal contact tracing data if they have such a right of access under any "rule of law or otherwise".

sections.label: Government Data Office investigates misuse
sections.summary: Disclosure or misuse of contact tracing data contravening the COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) Act will be investigated by authorised persons from the Government Data Office.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: If you peruse the Bill in front of you, you will realise that disclosure or misuse of contact tracing data on contravention of the COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) Act will be investigated by authorised persons from the Government Data Office appointed under this Act.

sections.label: Government Data Office oversight, no police
sections.summary: The Government Data Office will oversee public sector data governance policy and requirements, similar to PDPC for the private sector, and Police officers will not be appointed for this purpose.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: The Government Data Office will oversee the public sector data governance policy and requirements, similar to what the PDPC does for the private sector.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: And I can give this assurance that Police officers will not be appointed for this purpose.

sections.label: Disclosure report on data use
sections.summary: The Government accepts Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin's suggestion to publish a report disclosing use of the data beyond contact tracing.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin asked if the Government would consider publishing disclosure reports to help the public understand how the data is being used.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: We will accept Ms Nadia’s suggestion to have a report disclosing the use of the data beyond contact tracing.

sections.label: Balance on contact tracing data
sections.summary: The decision to include only serious offences and tightly scope personal contact tracing data balances public health, public security and personal data sensitivity.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Mr Pritam Singh, in his considered speech, also referred to the future and what impact these decisions may have.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I want to say that our decision today to only include serious offences, to tightly scope the use of personal contact tracing data is a result of a delicate balance between the right to public health, the right to public security and respecting the sensitivity of personal data during this extraordinary time.

sections.label: Bill not a precedent
sections.summary: The Bill seeks maximum public support against COVID-19 and is sui generis, moved under a Certificate of Urgency, and not a precedent.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: This Bill is about ensuring maximum support from the public in our fight against COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I want to stress this Bill is not a precedent.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: The nature of the legislation which this House is called upon to consider today is sui generis.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: It is a piece of legislation introduced during a public health crisis, being moved under a Certificate of Urgency, because of the situation that we are in.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: We are not trying to set a precedent here today.

sections.label: Minister's knowledge of CPC section
sections.summary: The Minister revealed he came to know section 20 of the CPC would apply from end October onwards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: The first being the Minister's revelation that he came to the knowledge that section 20 of the CPC would apply, from end October onwards.

sections.label: Question on 58% figure
sections.summary: A question is raised about the Minister's figure of 58% turning on TraceTogether at least once a day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: The second question I have pertains to a figure that Minister gave in his speech – 58% – and correct me if I am wrong, Minister, because I may have misheard you and I apologise for that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Fifty-eight percent turned on their TraceTogether at least once a day.

sections.label: TraceTogether devices and exchanges
sections.summary: As of now there are 31 to 35 TraceTogether devices around the speaker and 4,306 total exchanges today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: As of now, they are 31 to 35 TraceTogether devices around me and 4,306 total exchanges today.

sections.label: Carve-out for seven serious offences
sections.summary: The speaker asks for a carve-out for seven categories of serious offences so the Police Force is not unnecessarily restricted.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Because it was never designed for that purpose.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: But the reason why I am still coming to this House and still asking for this carve-out for the seven categories of serious offences, is really about a value statement – to say that for these types of situations, you do not believe in tying the hands of your Police Force unnecessarily.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: And even if you do not identify the suspect, it may help you identify a witness.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: So, what we are saying, in moving this Bill, is that, at least for these seven categories of serious crimes, let us agree not to tie the hands of our Police Force.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: And I am grateful to you and to the Workers' Party for saying you support this Bill.

sections.label: Trade-off on TT programme
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether leaders consider both sides, framing it as one victim versus thousands of possible TT programme drop-outs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: But when we are making a trade-off as leaders of the country, do we not actually think of both sides?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: It is about one victim versus thousands of possible drop-outs from the TT programme.

sections.label: Workers' Party position on Bill
sections.summary: The speaker says the Workers' Party took a responsible position that the Bill is necessary if exceptions exist for serious offences.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: In contrast to you, the Workers' Party – in my view and I hope you let me speak for you – has taken the more responsible position, that so long as you can envisage certain extreme, certain serious offences, for which you need to make an exception, then this Bill, with its current construction, is necessary.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: In fact, if you vote against the Bill, then the status quo applies and the status quo is that the CPC has licence over this data as well.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Singaporeans care, Singaporeans do look out for one another and Singaporeans will also accept that mistakes are made, but as long as you come clean and you explain why you did something, and you can convince them, and slowly step by step, win confidence, we can avoid these false dichotomies.
